events.label: Definition of parity
events.text: A written definition of parity with nine checks, and five rules: full fidelity, the rustty name, self-contained builds, an acyclic crate graph, and checks that are never weakened to pass.

events.label: Miri first
events.text: Miri adopted as the primary check for undefined behaviour and leaks; a custom tracking allocator was dropped.

events.label: Workflow scripts
events.text: Orchestration through workflow scripts: design, adversarial review, port, verify, one script per milestone with structured outputs.

events.label: Sanitizer matrix
events.text: A sanitizer check (ASan, LSan, MSan, TSan, HWASan), a Miri progress harness and a written route for tests Miri cannot run.

events.label: Raw-pointer arguments
events.text: Zig pointer arguments whose targets are re-read during a call are ported as raw pointers, after Miri caught a Stacked Borrows violation in screen clearing.

events.label: Placeholder leaves
events.text: Placeholder types with unimplemented leaves let most of the surface and app files port as live Rust before the GPU, event loop and inspector existed.

events.label: Scripts kept in the repo
events.text: Workflow scripts committed to the repository as executable provenance (61 on that day).

events.label: Miri proof harnesses
events.text: Small isolated Miri harnesses prove aliasing questions instead of reasoning about them by hand; a Tree Borrows lane is added.

events.label: Six new rules
events.text: Six new working rules: explicit semantics for replaced Zig primitives, compile-time stays compile-time, unsafe accounting, greppable port markers, separate implementer and reviewer, and tracking of every upstream commit.

events.label: Pointer-lifetime ledger
events.text: A retroactive ledger of who owns every pointer field (216 rows; its audit found 20 issues), and a checklist that requires ledger rows before any pointer-heavy part is ported.

events.label: Unsafe census
events.text: A committed script that counts every unsafe site, and a ledger of safe wrappers that are not yet sound.

events.label: First full engine Miri sweep
events.text: Miri over all 2,037 terminal-engine tests found a 9-test aliasing bug in search; it was fixed the same day, about 7 hours later.

events.label: Eight regression detectors
events.text: Eight detectors for known classes of port regressions: byte-slice reinterpretation, fixed-buffer capacity, folded constants, compile-time phases and emitted bytes, cross-crate invariants, a sanitizer canary, injected copies and stale comments.

events.label: Agent instructions
events.text: A committed file of build, test and Miri commands for agents.

events.label: Branches and merges
events.text: Branch-and-merge integration starts; the history was linear before.

events.label: Linux and a Linux VM
events.text: The Linux port starts, with a Linux virtual machine for GTK and OpenGL.

events.label: Completion roadmap
events.text: Twenty workstreams run by executors in isolated worktrees, each behind a review step.

events.label: Regular upstream catch-up
events.text: Moving the Ghostty reference commit forward becomes a recurring step: 8 moves absorbed 1,169 upstream non-merge commits.

events.label: False greens audited
events.text: A check that passed on bookkeeping alone is found; struck rows no longer vote, and a staleness check guards the unsafe census.

events.label: Second opinion from Codex
events.text: Codex's read-only audit (659 registry rows) is vetted by Claude: 144 findings confirmed, 3 refuted, 140 fixed and verified.

events.label: Move first
events.text: Move the reference first, record each check's state before and after, then port the difference.

events.label: Worktree subagents
events.text: Hand-made worktrees and agent workers replace the workflow scripts: 1,142 subagents in 214 worktrees in September.

events.label: Parity closure starts
events.text: Work starts on closing the 497 findings of a functional parity audit, each with a failing test first and a negative control.

events.label: Never port a bug
events.text: A Ghostty defect reachable from real input is fixed, tested with a negative control and recorded instead of ported; the defect ledger starts with 66 entries.

events.label: No silent skips
events.text: The never-port-a-bug rule is extended to non-crash bugs that break evident intent, and a test may no longer skip silently.

events.label: At most three building worktrees
events.text: About seven parallel agents filled the disk, so at most three worktrees build at once and each deletes its build output after merging.

events.label: Comments not carried
events.text: Every reference comment not carried into Rust is recorded with its reason.

events.label: Windows VM
events.text: A Windows 11 ARM64 virtual machine: the portable crates build and pass targeted tests on Windows.

events.label: Parity closure merged
events.text: The parity closure is merged with one low-severity item open; the parity check is a hard check.

events.label: Memory-safety lanes redesigned
events.text: Miri runs one process per test, plus Tree Borrows, LeakSanitizer on macOS and self-tests for every sanitizer.

events.label: Seventh reference move
events.text: The reference moves to a60e9e2a5, with an escape-sequence differential test against Ghostty.

events.label: Full run on one machine
events.text: The check script gains per-gate timings, a parallel scheduler with a cap on heavy checks, change-scoped long checks, sharded Valgrind and per-check build directories, so a full run fits on one machine.

events.label: Eighth reference move
events.text: Ghostty moved again during verification: the reference moves to 246f70287 (18 upstream commits, among them a soft terminal reset) and every reading check is green again 74 minutes later.

events.label: Final validation merged
events.text: The upstream catch-up is merged after a full validation at the current reference commit on macOS and the Linux VM, with the benchmarks re-run.

trigger.label: trigger
trigger.text: Trigger: Bun's write-up of its own Zig-to-Rust port was published on 07-08; ideas from it were adopted here on 07-10.
